responsible for making the final determination regarding an individual's eligibility for the benefit
sought. Id. In order to satisfy this criterion, the petitioner must establish not only that the beneficiary
has made original contributions but that they have been of major significance in the field. For example,
it may support the record with evidence that a beneficiary's contributions have been widely
implemented, have remarkably impacted or influenced the field, or have otherwise risen to a level of
major significance in the field. Demonstrating ability as a skilled systems architect is not itself a
contribution of major significance; rather, the Petitioner must demonstrate that the Beneficiary has
impacted the field as a whole. Cf Visinscaia, 4 F.Supp.3d at 134-35 (upholding a finding that a
ballroom dancer had not met a similar criterion in the regulations pertaining to immigrants of
extraordinary ability because she did not demonstrate her impact in the field as a whole).
Here, the preceding letters of recommendation demonstrate that the Beneficiary is admired for her
skills in the field of systems architecture, and that her work on projects has benefited her employers,
including the petitioning company, and earned the respect and admiration of those with whom she has
collaborated and consulted. The authors speak highly of the Beneficiary's work in systems

Based on the foregoing, the Petitioner has not established eligibility under this regulatory criterion.

Evidence that the alien has either commanded a high salary or will command a high
salary or other remuneration for services, evidenced by contracts or other reliable
evidence. 8 C.F.R. § 214.2(o)(3)(iii)(B)(8).
The Petitioner indicated on the petition that it has offered the Beneficiary an annual salary of $140,000
"plus bonus opportunities," for the proffered position of Principle Architect. However, within its response
to the Director's request for evidence it indicated the figure listed on the petition was incorrect, and was
copied mistakenly from the previous petition filed on the Beneficiary's behalf. The Petitioner's CFO
indicated the proffered base salary is $145,000, her salary at the time the petition was filed, and that she
regularly earns performance bonuses. It provided a paystub showing that her base salary at the time of
filing was $145,000, and her Form W-2, Wage and Tax Statement, for 2018 showing that her gross
pay was $163,051. The Petitioner has provided wage data for several different occupational titles, of
which the occupation of "Software Developers, Systems Software" appears to be the appropriate
classification for the Beneficiary's proffered position. According to the Bureau of Labor Statistics,
Occupational Employment Statistics, the 90th percentile wage reported for that occupation as of
May 2017 is $164,150. Based on national data for the relevant occupation and period, the Beneficiary
has commanded a high salary compared to similarly employed individuals. Therefore, we agree with the
Director's determination that the Petitioner satisfied this criterion.
